title: James Urish v. Rocky Mountain Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC answered the stated issue 'No'; it found no clear error and affirmed Presbytery's denial of the complaint. The complaint was therefore denied. No adopted ruling endorsed the candidate's disputed exegesis; the concurrence expressly disclaimed that the SJC was affirming the hendiadys view of 1 Tim. 2:12.
first_summary: The SJC denied a complaint against Rocky Mountain Presbytery's decision to sustain Dan Breed's ordination exam. Breed allowed women to teach Scripture to men and women under session oversight, though not to preach or hold office. Finding no clear error because the standards did not expressly address the view, the SJC affirmed the presbytery. A concurrence criticized Breed's exegesis but said the SJC did not endorse it.
summary: The SJC denied James Urish and others' complaint against Rocky Mountain Presbytery for sustaining Dan Breed's ordination exam. Breed had said women could teach Scripture to mixed adults in settings like Sunday school under session oversight, but not preach, hold elder office, or teach outside session authority. Because the Westminster Standards and BCO did not expressly resolve that view, the SJC found no clear error under BCO 39 and affirmed Presbytery's denial. A concurrence criticized Breed's exegesis of 1 Tim. 2:12 but stressed the SJC was not endorsing it.

evidence_notes.dispute: Complainants challenged Rocky Mountain Presbytery's January 23, 2009 action sustaining Dan Breed's theological and ordination examination after his statements about women teaching Scripture under session authority, excluding preaching and the elder office (lines 17–43).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC answered the issue 'No' (lines 47–53), found no clear error under BCO 39 and affirmed the presbytery's denial of the complaint (lines 57–81). The vote was 20 concur, 1 disqualified, 1 absent (lines 85–89).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The concurrence by RE Howard Donahoe, joined by TE Greco and RE Duncan, concurred in the judgment but criticized Breed's exegesis and stated the ruling did not affirm the hendiadys view of 1 Tim. 2:12 (lines 93–155).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No separate decision is incorporated by reference; the SJC's opinion is self-contained, and the BCO paragraphs cited are constitutional standards rather than incorporated case dispositions.
